LESSON: READING 14.4.1 FEATURES OF STYLE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Features of style
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 14.4.1 Features of style, part of Strand 14 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: where dialogues, similes, and metaphors can be used. Why do we use stylistic devices in writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online and offline for examples of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in stories and share them with the rest of the class,

2. read the class reader and identify with illustrations, instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text, and display their work on the class notice boards,

3. role-play selected dialogues from the class reader and record themselves for video sharing and review,

4. make sentences using the similes and metaphors identified from the text,

5. discuss instances in real life

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online and offline for examples of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in stories and share them with the rest of the class,
2. read the class reader and identify with illustrations, instances of dialogue, similes, and metaphors in the text, and display their work on the class notice boards,
3. role-play selected dialogues from the class reader and record themselves for video sharing and review,
4. make sentences using the similes and metaphors identified from the text,
5. discuss instances in real life

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Features of style together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: It is developed as the learner holds a discussion on instances in real life where dialogues, similes, and

metaphors can be used, thereby enhancing their literary skills.

• Learning to learn: It is achieved as the learner interacts with technology when recording and sharing videos of selected

dialogues from the class reader.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates others when role-playing selected dialogues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Critical thinking is achieved as the learner relates use of the features of styles in real life.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates features of style in the study of class readers to the learning of readers in Kiswahili.
